measurements.note: Corrected against the source: the sheet prints "> 100 %" for a carbon-filled polycarbonate, which cannot draw. As a bound it was asserting that the grade stretches at least 100 %, which under D55 would limit its own estimate from below.
Unit recovered from the raw value string: Spectrum PC-CF TDS reports flexural properties in kg/cm2 (technical-atmosphere units). Converted at 1 kg/cm2 = 0.0980665 MPa -> 90.2 MPa.

measurements.raw: 24 000 kg/cm2 (TDS prints "24.000" with European decimal separator)
measurements.note: Unit and magnitude recovered: TDS prints "24.000 kg/cm2"; the period is a European thousands separator, confirmed because 24 kg/cm2 (2.4 MPa) is physically impossible for a PC-CF flexural modulus. 24 000 kg/cm2 x 0.0980665 = 2354 MPa = 2.354 GPa, consistent with the 920 kg/cm2 (90.2 MPa) flexural strength in the same table.

measurements.note: Flagged physically implausible (D55): the sheet prints an elongation at break of 100 % for a carbon-fibre polycarbonate whose sheet prints a flexural modulus of 24,000 kg/cm² (2.4 GPa): short fibres stop a compound drawing past a few per cent. It reads as the neat resin's elongation. Kept as printed; it backs nothing.

measurements.note: The load was read: the page prints it as "4.6 kg/cm 2", 0.45 MPa, which the row had left out. Flagged as physically implausible: a polycarbonate bar is glassy, and its own sheet prints a glass transition of 120 °C (V013427, "Tg 120 °C"); a glassy bar cannot hold its shape 13 to 24 °C above it (CV64's margin is 15 °C, D149). One of the two figures is not this product's; it backs nothing until the maker says which.
